defects: The tabletop appears opaque and thick rather than thin smoked glass.
The drawer front and broad apron add a furniture style absent from the reference.
Four square supports and uniform near-black materials suppress the modern open-frame silhouette.
hard_fail_reasons: The candidate reads as chunky primitive furniture rather than the photographed thin glass desk with an exposed metal frame.
incumbent_comparison: First Art Factory candidate; compared with the existing legacy desk render. Not accepted.
likely_causes: The basic_rectangular_desk method delegates to the generic wood-furniture recipe, which adds drawers and a deep apron based on desk proportions.
The recipe assigns one dark color and rough material response to the entire asset, with no glass, graphite steel, or rubber separation.
next_action_hypothesis: Change the generation method to a dedicated low-profile computer-desk recipe: use a 0.7-inch smoked-glass slab with a readable beveled edge, four narrow graphite tubular legs, separate support rails and small satin mounting collars, rubber levelers, and no drawers or wood-like apron. Keep the exact 66 x 30 x 30-inch bounds and leave all RoomDefinition geometry untouched.

observations.art_direction_fit: The low-poly shading fits the room's broad style, but the old-fashioned drawer-heavy form does not fit the modern computer setup.
observations.close_up_quality: At close range the black slab and chunky square supports dominate; the asset loses its modern standing-desk construction.
observations.gameplay_readability: The desk remains legible beside the separate monitors and does not obscure their semantic identity.
observations.geometric_detail: The close view shows repeated rounded boxes and drawer fronts; it lacks thin edges, tubular supports, brackets, and glass mounts.
observations.material_realism: The tabletop renders as matte black wood-like material with no glass edge highlight or reflection.
observations.proportion: The tabletop is wide and low; the dark apron visually makes the body thicker than the reference.
observations.scale_fidelity: Godot measured the candidate bounds at exactly 66 x 30 x 30 inches, matching the RoomDefinition dimensions.
observations.semantic_recognizability: The 3/4 and profile production renders clearly read as a desk supporting the independently resolved monitors.
observations.silhouette_quality: The top and four legs are recognizable, but the apron and drawers form a heavy box silhouette unlike the reference's open support frame.
observations.source_resemblance: Sample (2) shows a thin black glass desktop on visible metal legs; v1 has a thick opaque top, panelled apron, drawers, and square legs.
observations.surface_variation: The tabletop and supports are nearly uniform black; material separation is weak.
observations.technical_integration: Godot imported 21 meshes and 21 surfaces; the production resolver loaded desk-v001 without fallback and the render run measured 47 FPS in its final close view.
